title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Macroeconomics vs Microeconomics
text:
Macroeconomics vs Microeconomics

Key terms: macroeconomics, microeconomics, inflation, unemployment

Macroeconomics focuses on the economy as a whole, while microeconomics studies individual markets and decision-makers. Macroeconomics deals with issues like inflation and unemployment, which microeconomics often takes as given.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Macroeconomics vs Microeconomics in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Aggregate Demand and Supply
text:
Aggregate Demand and Supply

Key terms: aggregate demand, aggregate supply, imaginary commodity

In macroeconomics, we often simplify analysis by focusing on a single imaginary commodity and its relationship with attributes like prices, interest rates, and wages, rather than studying individual commodities.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Aggregate Demand and Supply in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Economic Agents in Macroeconomics
text:
Economic Agents in Macroeconomics

Key terms: macroeconomic decision-makers, public goals, State, statutory bodies

Macroeconomic decision-makers are typically the State or statutory bodies like the Reserve Bank, pursuing public goals rather than individual self-interest.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Economic Agents in Macroeconomics in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Emergence of Macroeconomics
text:
Emergence of Macroeconomics

Key terms: John Maynard Keynes, The General Theory, Great Depression

Macroeconomics emerged as a separate branch of economics after John Maynard Keynes' 'The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money' was published in 1936, in response to the Great Depression.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Emergence of Macroeconomics in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Capitalist Economy
text:
Capitalist Economy

Key terms: capitalist enterprises, capital, land, labor, profit

In a capitalist economy, production activities are mainly carried out by capitalist enterprises, which use capital, land, and labor to produce goods and services, aiming to make a profit.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Capitalist Economy in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Factors of Production
text:
Factors of Production

Key terms: capital, land, labor, entrepreneur

Capital, land, and labor are the main factors of production in a capitalist economy. The entrepreneur combines these factors to produce goods and services, which are then sold in the market.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Factors of Production in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Revenue Distribution
text:
Revenue Distribution

Key terms: revenue, rent, interest, wages, profit

Revenue earned from selling products is distributed among the factors of production: rent for land, interest for capital, wages for labor, and the rest is profit for the entrepreneur.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Revenue Distribution in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Investment Expenditure
text:
Investment Expenditure

Key terms: investment, expenditure, production, expansion

Profits earned by entrepreneurs can be used to buy new machinery or build new factories, which are examples of investment expenditure that can expand production.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Investment Expenditure in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Capitalist Economy Definition
text:
Capitalist Economy Definition

Key terms: capitalist, economy, private ownership, market, wage rate

A capitalist economy is characterized by private ownership of means of production, production for selling in the market, and the sale and purchase of labor services at a wage rate.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Capitalist Economy Definition in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Wage Labour
text:
Wage Labour

Key terms: wage labour, wages, capitalist economies

Wage labour refers to labor that is sold and purchased against wages. It is a common feature of capitalist economies.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Wage Labour in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Firm in a Capitalist Economy
text:
Firm in a Capitalist Economy

Key terms: firm, entrepreneur, wage labor, capital, land, market, profits

In a firm, the entrepreneur hires wage labor, employs the services of capital and land, and undertakes production to sell goods and services in the market and earn profits.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Firm in a Capitalist Economy in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Role of the State in an Economy
text:
Role of the State in an Economy

Key terms: state, laws, justice, production, taxes, infrastructure, services

The state plays a role in framing laws, enforcing them, delivering justice, and undertaking production, as well as imposing taxes and spending money on public infrastructure and services.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Role of the State in an Economy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Role of the State in an Economy in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Household Sector in an Economy
text:
Household Sector in an Economy

Key terms: household, consumption, savings, taxes, income, firms, government

The household sector consists of individuals or groups who make decisions about their own consumption, savings, and taxes. They earn income through working in firms, government, or owning firms.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Household Sector in an Economy in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Final Goods vs. Intermediate Goods
text:
Final Goods vs. Intermediate Goods

Key terms: Final Goods, Intermediate Goods, GDP

Final goods are meant for end-use (consumption or investment), while intermediate goods are used in production of other goods. Only final goods are counted in GDP.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Final Goods vs. Intermediate Goods in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Consumption Goods vs. Capital Goods
text:
Consumption Goods vs. Capital Goods

Key terms: Consumption Goods, Capital Goods, Final Goods

Consumption goods are for immediate use (like food, clothing), while capital goods are used in production (like machines, buildings). Both are final goods.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Consumption Goods vs. Capital Goods in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Consumer Durables
text:
Consumer Durables

Key terms: Consumer Durables, Final Goods, Capital Goods

Consumer durables are long-lasting goods bought for consumption, like cars or TVs. They are also final goods but have characteristics of capital goods.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Consumer Durables in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Stocks vs. Flows
text:
Stocks vs. Flows

Key terms: Stocks, Flows, GDP

Stocks are quantities at a specific point in time (like capital stock), while flows occur over a period (like GDP).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Stocks vs. Flows in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Gross Investment vs. Net Investment
text:
Gross Investment vs. Net Investment

Key terms: Gross Investment, Net Investment, Depreciation

Gross investment is the total value of capital goods produced, while net investment is gross investment minus depreciation (wear and tear).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Gross Investment vs. Net Investment in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Depreciation
text:
Depreciation

Key terms: Depreciation, Capital Good, Useful Life

Depreciation is the annual allowance for wear and tear of a capital good, calculated as the cost of the good divided by its useful life.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Depreciation in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Steady Replacement Spending
text:
Steady Replacement Spending

Key terms: depreciation, replacement spending, capital

Assumes a constant flow of spending to replace depreciated capital, matching annual depreciation.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Steady Replacement Spending in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Consumer vs Capital Goods Production
text:
Consumer vs Capital Goods Production

Key terms: consumer goods, capital goods, trade-off

Economy produces either consumer goods (for people) or capital goods (for businesses), with a trade-off between the two.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Consumer vs Capital Goods Production in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Capital Goods and Production
text:
Capital Goods and Production

Key terms: capital goods, labor productivity, consumer goods

More advanced capital goods increase labor productivity, leading to higher consumer goods production in the future.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Capital Goods and Production in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Depreciation Calculation
text:
Depreciation Calculation

Key terms: depreciation, asset, constant rate

Depreciation is calculated based on the original value of an asset, assuming a constant rate of depreciation.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Depreciation Calculation in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Circular Flow of Income
text:
Circular Flow of Income

Key terms: income, consumption, production, circular flow

Income generated from production enables consumption, which in turn drives further production, creating a circular flow.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Circular Flow of Income in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | National Income Calculation Methods
text:
National Income Calculation Methods

Key terms: national income, expenditure method, product method, income method

National income can be calculated using the expenditure, product, or income method, with the same result.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to National Income Calculation Methods in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Aggregate Spending and Income
text:
Aggregate Spending and Income

Key terms: aggregate spending, income, economy

An increase in aggregate spending leads to an equivalent increase in income, allowing the economy to support the higher spending level.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Aggregate Spending and Income in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Value Added
text:
Value Added

Key terms: Value Added, Intermediate Goods

The net contribution made by a firm after subtracting the value of intermediate goods used in production.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Value Added in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Gross Value Added (GVA)
text:
Gross Value Added (GVA)

Key terms: Gross Value Added, Depreciation

The value of production of a firm minus the value of intermediate goods used, including depreciation.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gross Value Added (GVA) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Net Value Added (NVA)
text:
Net Value Added (NVA)

Key terms: Net Value Added, Depreciation

Gross Value Added minus depreciation, representing the firm's net contribution to the economy.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Net Value Added (NVA) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Inventory
text:
Inventory

Key terms: Inventory, Stock

Stock of unsold finished goods, semi-finished goods, or raw materials that a firm carries from one year to the next.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Inventory in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
text:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP)

Key terms: GDP, Gross Value Added

The total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given year.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Expenditure Method for GDP
text:
Expenditure Method for GDP

Key terms: Expenditure Method, GDP, Final Expenditure

Calculating GDP by adding final expenditures made by households, firms, government, and foreign buyers.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Expenditure Method for GDP in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
text:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP)

Key terms: GDP, market prices, final goods, services

GDP measures the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period, usually a year. It includes all final goods and services produced by both residents and non-residents, valued at market prices.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GDP by Expenditure Method
text:
GDP by Expenditure Method

Key terms: expenditure method, C, I, G, X, M

GDP can be calculated by adding up the total expenditure on final goods and services by consumers (C), businesses (I), government (G), and foreigners (X), then subtracting the expenditure on imports (M).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to GDP by Expenditure Method in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GDP by Income Method
text:
GDP by Income Method

Key terms: income method, W, P, In, R

GDP can also be calculated by adding up the total income received by all factors of production, including wages (W), profits (P), interest (In), and rents (R).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to GDP by Income Method in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Gross National Product (GNP)
text:
Gross National Product (GNP)

Key terms: GNP, net factor income from abroad

GNP adjusts GDP for net factor income from abroad, which accounts for the earnings of domestic factors of production employed abroad and the earnings of foreign factors of production employed domestically.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gross National Product (GNP) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Net National Product (NNP)
text:
Net National Product (NNP)

Key terms: NNP, depreciation

NNP is calculated by subtracting depreciation from GNP. It represents the total value of goods and services produced, minus the value of capital used up in the production process.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Net National Product (NNP) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | National Income (NI)
text:
National Income (NI)

Key terms: NI, net indirect taxes

National Income is calculated by subtracting net indirect taxes from NNP at market prices. It represents the total income earned by all factors of production in the economy.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to National Income (NI) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Personal Income (PI)
text:
Personal Income (PI)

Key terms: PI, undistributed profits, net interest payments, corporate tax, transfer payments

PI is calculated by subtracting undistributed profits, net interest payments, corporate tax, and adding transfer payments to households from NI. It represents the total income received by households.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Personal Income (PI) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Personal Disposable Income (PDI)
text:
Personal Disposable Income (PDI)

Key terms: PDI, personal tax payments, non-tax payments

PDI is calculated by subtracting personal tax payments and non-tax payments from PI. It represents the total income that households have discretion over, after taxes and other obligations.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Personal Disposable Income (PDI) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
text:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP)

Key terms: GDP, market prices, final goods and services

The total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year, measured at market prices.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GDP at Factor Cost
text:
GDP at Factor Cost

Key terms: GDP at factor cost, factor prices, indirect taxes, subsidies

GDP measured at the prices received by producers, excluding indirect taxes and including subsidies.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to GDP at Factor Cost in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Net Domestic Product (NDP)
text:
Net Domestic Product (NDP)

Key terms: NDP, depreciation, factor income

GDP minus depreciation, representing the total income earned by factors of production within a country.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Net Domestic Product (NDP) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Gross National Product (GNP)
text:
Gross National Product (GNP)

Key terms: GNP, national residents, production abroad

The total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, regardless of where the production takes place.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gross National Product (GNP) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Real GDP
text:
Real GDP

Key terms: real GDP, inflation adjustment, constant prices

GDP adjusted for inflation, allowing comparison of production levels over time.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Real GDP in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GDP Deflator
text:
GDP Deflator

Key terms: GDP deflator, price index, inflation

An index that measures the average change in price of all goods and services included in GDP.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to GDP Deflator in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Consumer Price Index (CPI)
text:
Consumer Price Index (CPI)

Key terms: CPI, consumer basket, price change

A measure of the average change in prices of a fixed basket of goods and services purchased by consumers.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Consumer Price Index (CPI) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GDP and Welfare
text:
GDP and Welfare

Key terms: GDP, welfare, income distribution, externalities

GDP is not a perfect measure of a country's well-being due to factors like income distribution, non-monetary exchanges, and externalities.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to GDP and Welfare in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Factor Payments and Income Measurement
text:
Factor Payments and Income Measurement

Key terms: factor payments, product method, expenditure method

Economies measure income using three methods: factor payments (income), product (value of goods/services produced), and expenditure (value of spending received). The product method avoids double-counting by only including final goods and services.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Factor Payments and Income Measurement in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Gross Investment and Net Investment
text:
Gross Investment and Net Investment

Key terms: gross investment, net investment, depreciation

Gross investment is the total value of new capital goods bought by firms. Net investment is gross investment minus depreciation, representing the actual increase in the capital stock.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Gross Investment and Net Investment in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Stocks vs Flows
text:
Stocks vs Flows

Key terms: stocks, flows, capital stock, investment

Stocks represent a quantity at a specific point in time (e.g., capital stock), while flows represent a quantity over a period (e.g., investment).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Stocks vs Flows in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GDP, GNP, NNP
text:
GDP, GNP, NNP

Key terms: GDP, GNP, NNP, depreciation

GDP measures the value of goods and services produced within a country's borders. GNP includes income earned by residents abroad. NNP subtracts depreciation from GDP or GNP.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to GDP, GNP, NNP in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Price Indices: GDP Deflator, CPI, WPI
text:
Price Indices: GDP Deflator, CPI, WPI

Key terms: GDP deflator, CPI, WPI

Price indices (GDP deflator, CPI, WPI) measure changes in the general price level. The GDP deflator uses GDP as the base, CPI focuses on consumer goods, and WPI tracks wholesale prices.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Price Indices: GDP Deflator, CPI, WPI
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Price Indices: GDP Deflator, CPI, WPI in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GDP as a Welfare Indicator
text:
GDP as a Welfare Indicator

Key terms: GDP, welfare, non-market activities, environmental impacts

GDP is not a perfect measure of a country's welfare. It excludes non-market activities, environmental impacts, and income inequality.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to GDP as a Welfare Indicator in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Budget Deficit and Trade Deficit
text:
Budget Deficit and Trade Deficit

Key terms: budget deficit, trade deficit, government spending, imports, exports

Budget deficit occurs when a government spends more than it earns. Trade deficit happens when a country imports more than it exports.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Budget Deficit and Trade Deficit in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Inventory Accumulation
text:
Inventory Accumulation

Key terms: inventory, planned accumulation, unplanned accumulation, demand, supply

Planned inventory accumulation occurs when firms intentionally increase their stock levels. Unplanned accumulation happens due to unexpected changes in demand or supply.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Inventory Accumulation in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Role of Money in Economy
text:
Role of Money in Economy

Key terms: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value

Money serves as a medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value, making transactions easier and more efficient.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Role of Money in Economy in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Barter System Limitations
text:
Barter System Limitations

Key terms: double coincidence of wants, search costs

Barter systems have limitations such as the double coincidence of wants and high search costs, making money a necessary facilitator of transactions.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Barter System Limitations in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Money Creation by Banks
text:
Money Creation by Banks

Key terms: credit creation, money multiplier

Banks create money by lending to customers, who then deposit the loans back into the bank, increasing the money supply.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Money Creation by Banks in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)
text:
Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)

Key terms: Cash Reserve Ratio, required reserve ratio

The CRR is a legal requirement for banks to maintain a certain percentage of deposits as cash reserves, limiting their ability to create money.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Central Bank's Role in Money Supply
text:
Central Bank's Role in Money Supply

Key terms: central bank, money supply, bank rate, open market operations

Central banks control money supply through methods like bank rate, open market operations, and variations in reserve ratios.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Central Bank's Role in Money Supply
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Central Bank's Role in Money Supply in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Cashless Society
text:
Cashless Society

Key terms: cashless society, digital transactions, financial inclusion

A cashless society uses digital transactions instead of physical money, promoting financial inclusion and convenience.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Cashless Society in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)
text:
Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)

Key terms: Cash Reserve Ratio, Central bank, reserves, over lending

A percentage of deposits that banks must keep as cash reserves with the bank, determined by the Central bank (RBI) to prevent 'over lending'.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Money Multiplier Process
text:
Money Multiplier Process

Key terms: money multiplier, deposits, lending, money supply

A process where initial deposits in a bank can lead to a multiple increase in the money supply through lending and re-depositing.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Money Multiplier Process in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
text:
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)

Key terms: Statutory Liquidity Ratio, liquid assets, deposits

A requirement for banks to keep a certain portion of their deposits in liquid form, in addition to the CRR.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Bank Rate
text:
Bank Rate

Key terms: Bank Rate, Central bank, commercial banks, money supply

The rate at which the Central bank lends money to commercial banks, influencing the money supply by making loans more or less expensive.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Bank Rate in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Open Market Operations
text:
Open Market Operations

Key terms: Open Market Operations, Central bank, government bonds, money supply

A tool used by the Central bank to control money supply by buying or selling government bonds in the open market.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Open Market Operations in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Transaction Demand for Money
text:
Transaction Demand for Money

Key terms: transaction demand for money, value of transactions, velocity of circulation

The amount of money held by individuals and businesses for day-to-day transactions, determined by the value of transactions and the velocity of circulation.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Transaction Demand for Money in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Speculative Demand for Money
text:
Speculative Demand for Money

Key terms: speculative demand for money, interest rates, alternative assets

The amount of money held by individuals for potential investment opportunities, influenced by interest rates and expected returns on alternative assets.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Speculative Demand for Money in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Present Value of a Bond
text:
Present Value of a Bond

Key terms: Present Value, Bond, Interest Rate

The present value of a bond is the amount you'd need to invest today to get the future stream of returns from the bond. It's calculated using the formula: PV = X + Y = 100 / (1 + r)^n, where X and Y are the annual returns, r is the interest rate, and n is the number of years.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Present Value of a Bond in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Bond Price and Interest Rate Relationship
text:
Bond Price and Interest Rate Relationship

Key terms: Bond Price, Interest Rate, Inverse Relationship

The price of a bond is inversely related to the market rate of interest. This means that when the interest rate increases, the price of the bond decreases, and vice versa. This is because a higher interest rate makes bonds less attractive, as investors can get a higher return from other investments.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Bond Price and Interest Rate Relationship
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Bond Price and Interest Rate Relationship in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Speculative Demand for Money
text:
Speculative Demand for Money

Key terms: Speculative Demand, Money, Interest Rate

Speculative demand for money refers to the desire to hold money for the purpose of making capital gains or avoiding capital losses from changes in the price of bonds. It's inversely related to the interest rate, meaning that when the interest rate is high, people expect it to fall in the future, so they hold money instead of bonds.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Speculative Demand for Money in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Liquidity Trap
text:
Liquidity Trap

Key terms: Liquidity Trap, Interest Rate, Money

A liquidity trap is a situation where people prefer to hold money rather than invest it, even when the interest rate is very low. This happens when people expect the interest rate to rise in the future, causing capital losses on bonds. In this situation, injecting more money into the economy won't lower the interest rate further.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Liquidity Trap in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Narrow and Broad Money
text:
Narrow and Broad Money

Key terms: Narrow Money, Broad Money, Liquidity

Narrow money (M1 and M2) refers to money that is easily convertible into cash, like currency notes and coins, and demand deposits. Broad money (M3 and M4) includes narrow money plus less liquid assets like time deposits and shares. M1 is the most liquid, while M4 is the least liquid.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Narrow and Broad Money in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Fiat Money
text:
Fiat Money

Key terms: Fiat Money, Legal Tender

Fiat money is a type of currency declared legal tender by a government but not backed by a physical commodity. Its value comes from the collective faith of its users and the stability of the issuing government. Legal tender refers to a currency that must be accepted as payment for debts.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fiat Money in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Money Multiplier
text:
Money Multiplier

Key terms: Money Multiplier, Reserve Ratio, Cash Ratio

The money multiplier is a measure of how much money a bank can create from a given deposit. It's calculated as 1 / (reserve ratio + cash ratio). The money multiplier determines how much the money supply will increase for a given increase in the excess reserves of banks.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Money Multiplier in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Monetary Policy Instruments
text:
Monetary Policy Instruments

Key terms: Monetary Policy, Instruments, Central Bank

Monetary policy instruments are tools used by a central bank to influence the money supply and interest rates. Examples include open market operations, bank rate, cash reserve ratio, repo rate, and reverse repo rate. These instruments allow the central bank to control the money supply and influence the economy.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Monetary Policy Instruments in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Monetary Base Components
text:
Monetary Base Components

Key terms: currency in circulation, bank reserves, monetary base

The monetary base consists of currency in circulation and bank reserves held with the central bank. These components change over time.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Monetary Base Components in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Changes in Monetary Base
text:
Changes in Monetary Base

Key terms: increase, decrease, currency, deposits

The monetary base can increase or decrease due to changes in currency held by the public and deposits held by commercial banks with the central bank.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Changes in Monetary Base in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Time Deposits and Monetary Base
text:
Time Deposits and Monetary Base

Key terms: time deposits, commercial banks, monetary base

Time deposits held by commercial banks can affect the monetary base. When these deposits increase, the monetary base also tends to increase.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Time Deposits and Monetary Base in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Monetary Base Growth Over Time
text:
Monetary Base Growth Over Time

Key terms: growth, monetary base, time

The monetary base has been growing over time, as shown by the increasing values in the given table from 1981-82 to 2024-25.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Monetary Base Growth Over Time in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Ex Ante vs Ex Post Measures
text:
Ex Ante vs Ex Post Measures

Key terms: Ex Ante, Ex Post, Planned Values, Actual Values

Ex ante measures are planned values of variables like consumption, investment, or output, while ex post measures are actual values. Understanding this difference is crucial for analyzing economic behavior.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Ex Ante vs Ex Post Measures
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ex Ante vs Ex Post Measures in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Consumption Function
text:
Consumption Function

Key terms: Consumption Function, Autonomous Consumption, Marginal Propensity to Consume

The consumption function (C = C + cY) describes the relationship between consumption (C) and income (Y), with autonomous consumption (C) and marginal propensity to consume (c).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Consumption Function in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC)
text:
Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC)

Key terms: Marginal Propensity to Consume, MPC

MPC is the change in consumption per unit change in income. It's a measure of how much additional consumption arises from an additional unit of income.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS)
text:
Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS)

Key terms: Marginal Propensity to Save, MPS

MPS is the change in savings per unit change in income. It's a measure of how much additional savings arise from an additional unit of income.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Aggregate Demand (AD)
text:
Aggregate Demand (AD)

Key terms: Aggregate Demand, AD, Consumption, Investment, Government Expenditure, Taxes

AD is the sum of planned consumption (C) and planned investment (I), plus government expenditure (G) minus taxes (T). It's the total demand for goods and services in the economy.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Aggregate Demand (AD) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Macroeconomic Equilibrium (Fixed Price Level)
text:
Macroeconomic Equilibrium (Fixed Price Level)

Key terms: Macroeconomic Equilibrium, Price Level, Simplifying Assumption

In macroeconomic theory, equilibrium is first analyzed with the price level fixed. This is a simplifying assumption that allows us to focus on the determination of income and employment.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Macroeconomic Equilibrium (Fixed Price Level) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Consumption Function
text:
Consumption Function

Key terms: Consumption, Income, Marginal Propensity to Consume

Consumption (C) is a function of income (Y), with a constant 'C' (intercept) and a slope 'c' (marginal propensity to consume).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Consumption Function in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Investment Function
text:
Investment Function

Key terms: Investment, Autonomous

Investment (I) is autonomous, meaning it's the same regardless of income level, and is represented as a horizontal line in a graph.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Investment Function in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Aggregate Demand
text:
Aggregate Demand

Key terms: Aggregate Demand, Consumption, Investment

Aggregate Demand (AD) is the total demand for goods and services in an economy, calculated by adding consumption and investment.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Aggregate Demand in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Macroeconomic Equilibrium
text:
Macroeconomic Equilibrium

Key terms: Macroeconomic Equilibrium, Ex Ante Aggregate Demand, Ex Ante Aggregate Supply

Macroeconomic Equilibrium occurs when Ex Ante Aggregate Demand equals Ex Ante Aggregate Supply, resulting in a stable economy.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Macroeconomic Equilibrium in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Multiplier Effect
text:
Multiplier Effect

Key terms: Multiplier Effect, Autonomous Expenditure, Equilibrium Income, Equilibrium Output

The Multiplier Effect is a mechanism where an initial change in autonomous expenditure leads to a larger change in equilibrium income and output.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Multiplier Effect in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Paradox of Thrift
text:
Paradox of Thrift

Key terms: Paradox of Thrift, Multiplier Effect, Savings

The Paradox of Thrift states that if everyone tries to save more, total savings may not increase, or could even decrease, due to the multiplier effect.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Paradox of Thrift in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Aggregate Demand (AD) Shift
text:
Aggregate Demand (AD) Shift

Key terms: Aggregate Demand, Marginal Propensity to Consume, Autonomous Expenditure, Equilibrium Output

A change in the marginal propensity to consume (mpc) or autonomous expenditure (A) causes the AD line to shift, affecting equilibrium output (Y).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Aggregate Demand (AD) Shift in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Paradox of Thrift
text:
Paradox of Thrift

Key terms: Savings, Marginal Propensity to Consume, Aggregate Demand, Output

An increase in savings (due to a decrease in mpc) reduces aggregate demand, leading to a decrease in output and savings, contradicting the initial intention to increase savings.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Paradox of Thrift in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Equilibrium Output and Employment
text:
Equilibrium Output and Employment

Key terms: Equilibrium Output, Full Employment, Deficient Demand, Excess Demand, Prices

The equilibrium output, where Y = AD, does not guarantee full employment. It may lead to deficient or excess demand, affecting prices in the long run.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Equilibrium Output and Employment in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Marginal Propensity to Consume (mpc)
text:
Marginal Propensity to Consume (mpc)

Key terms: Marginal Propensity to Consume, Marginal Propensity to Save

The rate at which consumption increases with a unit increase in income. It's related to marginal propensity to save (mps) as mpc + mps = 1.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Marginal Propensity to Consume (mpc) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Ex Ante vs Ex Post Investment
text:
Ex Ante vs Ex Post Investment

Key terms: Ex Ante Investment, Ex Post Investment, Unintended Changes in Inventories

Ex ante investment is planned investment, while ex post investment is actual investment. They may differ due to unintended changes in inventories.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Ex Ante vs Ex Post Investment
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ex Ante vs Ex Post Investment in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Effective Demand Principle
text:
Effective Demand Principle

Key terms: Effective Demand, Aggregate Demand, Aggregate Supply

In the short run, with a constant price and interest rate, aggregate output is determined solely by aggregate demand.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Effective Demand Principle in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Autonomous Expenditure Multiplier
text:
Autonomous Expenditure Multiplier

Key terms: Autonomous Expenditure, Multiplier Effect, Marginal Propensity to Consume

The multiplier effect of an increase in autonomous expenditure on equilibrium output, calculated as 1 / (1 - mpc).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Autonomous Expenditure Multiplier in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Parametric Shift of a Line
text:
Parametric Shift of a Line

Key terms: Parametric Shift, Slope, Intercept, Aggregate Demand, Aggregate Supply

A change in the slope (mpc) or intercept (A) of a line (AD) causes it to shift, affecting its intersection with the Y-axis or another line (AS).

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Parametric Shift of a Line in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Government Budget Components
text:
Government Budget Components

Key terms: revenue receipts, capital receipts, revenue expenditure, capital expenditure

The government budget consists of revenue and capital receipts, and revenue and capital expenditures. Revenue receipts are non-redeemable and include taxes and non-tax revenues, while capital receipts create liability or reduce financial assets. Revenue expenditures are for normal functioning, while capital expenditures create physical or financial assets.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Government Budget Components in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Public Goods and Government Role
text:
Public Goods and Government Role

Key terms: public goods, non-excludable, government allocation function

Public goods, like national defense and roads, benefit everyone and are non-excludable. The government provides these goods as it's the only entity that can ensure everyone pays for and has access to them.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Public Goods and Government Role in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Government Redistribution Function
text:
Government Redistribution Function

Key terms: redistribution, taxes, transfers, income distribution

The government redistributes income through taxes and transfers to achieve a fairer income distribution. It collects taxes from households and firms, then redistributes through transfers like subsidies and welfare programs.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Government Redistribution Function in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Government Stabilisation Function
text:
Government Stabilisation Function

Key terms: stabilisation, aggregate demand, full employment, inflation

The government stabilises the economy by adjusting aggregate demand. It can increase demand through spending or decrease it through tax increases to maintain full employment and control inflation.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Government Stabilisation Function in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Balanced, Surplus, and Deficit Budgets
text:
Balanced, Surplus, and Deficit Budgets

Key terms: balanced budget, surplus, deficit

A balanced budget occurs when revenue equals expenditure. A surplus occurs when revenue exceeds expenditure, and a deficit occurs when expenditure exceeds revenue.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Balanced, Surplus, and Deficit Budgets in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Budget Deficit Implications and Measures
text:
Budget Deficit Implications and Measures

Key terms: budget deficit, government debt, interest payments, debt management

Budget deficits can lead to increased government debt and higher interest payments. Measures to contain deficits include reducing expenditure, increasing revenue, or using debt management strategies.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Budget Deficit Implications and Measures in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Revenue Deficit
text:
Revenue Deficit

Key terms: revenue expenditure, revenue receipts, budget deficit

Excess of government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts. It's like when you spend more than you earn, but only considering your income and expenses that affect your current financial situation.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Revenue Deficit in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Fiscal Deficit
text:
Fiscal Deficit

Key terms: total expenditure, total receipts, borrowing

Difference between government's total expenditure and its total receipts, excluding borrowing. It's like when you spend more than you earn, including your savings and loans.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fiscal Deficit in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Primary Deficit
text:
Primary Deficit

Key terms: fiscal deficit, interest payments, current fiscal imbalances

Fiscal deficit minus interest payments. It focuses on the current fiscal imbalances, ignoring the interest on accumulated debt.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Primary Deficit in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Government Budget and the Economy
text:
Government Budget and the Economy

Key terms: equilibrium income, government purchases, taxes, transfers

The government's budget directly affects the level of equilibrium income in two ways: through government purchases of goods and services, and through taxes and transfers that affect the relation between income and disposable income.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Government Budget and the Economy in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Government Expenditure Multiplier
text:
Government Expenditure Multiplier

Key terms: equilibrium income, government spending, multiplier

The change in equilibrium income caused by a change in government spending. It's like how much more you'll earn if your government spends more money.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Government Expenditure Multiplier in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Tax Multiplier
text:
Tax Multiplier

Key terms: equilibrium income, taxes, multiplier

The change in equilibrium income caused by a change in taxes. It's like how much more you'll earn if the government cuts taxes.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Tax Multiplier in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Balanced Budget Multiplier
text:
Balanced Budget Multiplier

Key terms: equilibrium income, government spending, taxes, balanced budget

The change in equilibrium income when an increase in government spending is matched by an equal increase in taxes, keeping the budget balanced. It's like how much more you'll earn if the government spends more money, but also collects more taxes to balance the budget.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Balanced Budget Multiplier in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Aggregate Demand with Proportional Taxes
text:
Aggregate Demand with Proportional Taxes

Key terms: Aggregate Demand, Proportional Taxes, Multiplier Effect

Aggregate demand (AD) curve becomes flatter with proportional taxes, reducing the multiplier effect of government expenditure and consumption.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Aggregate Demand with Proportional Taxes in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Income Tax as an Automatic Stabiliser
text:
Income Tax as an Automatic Stabiliser

Key terms: Income Tax, Automatic Stabiliser, Disposable Income

Income tax acts as an automatic stabiliser, making disposable income and consumer spending less sensitive to GDP fluctuations.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Income Tax as an Automatic Stabiliser
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Income Tax as an Automatic Stabiliser in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Government Budget and the Economy
text:
Government Budget and the Economy

Key terms: Government Budget, Economic Influence, Allocation, Redistribution, Stabilisation

The government's budget, consisting of receipts and expenditure, influences the economy through allocation, redistribution, and stabilisation.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Government Budget and the Economy in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Public Goods and Government Provision
text:
Public Goods and Government Provision

Key terms: Public Goods, Non-Rivalrous, Non-Excludable, Government Provision

Public goods, being non-rivalrous and non-excludable, are collectively consumed and must be provided by the government as private enterprise won't.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Public Goods and Government Provision in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Fiscal Policy Instruments for Economic Stabilisation
text:
Fiscal Policy Instruments for Economic Stabilisation

Key terms: Fiscal Policy, Economic Stabilisation, Government Expenditure, Taxes

Fiscal policy instruments like government expenditure and taxes can be varied to offset undesirable shifts in investment demand, stabilising the economy.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Fiscal Policy Instruments for Economic Stabilisation
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Fiscal Policy Instruments for Economic Stabilisation in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Ricardian Equivalence
text:
Ricardian Equivalence

Key terms: Ricardian Equivalence, Consumer Behaviour, Taxation, Borrowing

Ricardian equivalence argues that consumers save more in the face of high deficits, making taxation and borrowing equivalent means of financing expenditure.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Ricardian Equivalence in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Government Debt and Burden on Future Generations
text:
Government Debt and Burden on Future Generations

Key terms: Government Debt, Burden, Future Generations, Output Growth

Government debt can be burdensome if it reduces future growth in output, as it may transfer the burden of reduced consumption to future generations.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Government Debt and Burden on Future Generations
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Government Debt and Burden on Future Generations in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Fiscal Policy Principles of FRBM Act
text:
Fiscal Policy Principles of FRBM Act

Key terms: Fiscal Policy, FRBM Act, Fiscal Deficit, Revenue Surplus

The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBM) sets rules for the government to maintain fiscal prudence, ensuring inter-generational equity and macro-economic stability by limiting deficits and borrowing.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Fiscal Policy Principles of FRBM Act
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fiscal Policy Principles of FRBM Act in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Fiscal Deficit Reduction Targets
text:
Fiscal Deficit Reduction Targets

Key terms: Fiscal Deficit, Revenue Deficit, GDP, FRBM Act

The FRBM Act mandates the central government to reduce fiscal deficit to not more than 3% of GDP and eliminate revenue deficit by 2009, with annual reductions of 0.3% and 0.5% respectively.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Fiscal Deficit Reduction Targets in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Exceptions to Fiscal Deficit Targets
text:
Exceptions to Fiscal Deficit Targets

Key terms: Fiscal Deficit, Exceptions, National Security, Natural Calamity

The central government can exceed fiscal deficit targets only on grounds of national security, natural calamity, or other exceptional grounds specified by the government.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Exceptions to Fiscal Deficit Targets in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Government Borrowing Restrictions
text:
Government Borrowing Restrictions

Key terms: Government Borrowing, Reserve Bank of India, FRBM Act

The FRBM Act restricts the central government from borrowing from the Reserve Bank of India except for temporary cash flow needs and prohibits the Reserve Bank from subscribing to primary issues of government securities from 2006-07.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Government Borrowing Restrictions in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Transparency in Fiscal Operations
text:
Transparency in Fiscal Operations

Key terms: Transparency, Fiscal Operations, Parliament, Quarterly Reviews

The FRBM Act requires the central government to take measures to ensure greater transparency in fiscal operations, including laying statements before Parliament and quarterly reviews of receipts and expenditure.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Transparency in Fiscal Operations in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GST: One Nation, One Tax, One Market
text:
GST: One Nation, One Tax, One Market

Key terms: GST, Indirect Tax, Common Market, Business Operations

Goods and Service Tax (GST) is a single, comprehensive indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, aiming to create a common market in India by reducing the cost of business operations and cascading effect of taxes.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: GST: One Nation, One Tax, One Market
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to GST: One Nation, One Tax, One Market in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GST Rates and Exemptions
text:
GST Rates and Exemptions

Key terms: GST Rates, Exemptions, Petroleum Products, Alcoholic Liquor, Tobacco

GST has six standard rates (0%, 3%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%) and exempts certain petroleum products, alcoholic liquor, and tobacco. It subsumes various Central and State taxes and cesses.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to GST Rates and Exemptions in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | GST Benefits and Challenges
text:
GST Benefits and Challenges

Key terms: GST Benefits, Tax Burden, Business Adaptation

GST simplifies the tax system, reduces costs, and expands the tax base. However, it may initially increase the overall tax burden and require businesses to adapt to new procedures.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to GST Benefits and Challenges in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Open Economy
text:
Open Economy

Key terms: Open Economy, Trade, Financial Assets

An open economy interacts with other countries through trade in goods, services, and financial assets, unlike a closed economy that doesn't consider international linkages.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Open Economy in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Balance of Payments (BoP)
text:
Balance of Payments (BoP)

Key terms: Balance of Payments, Current Account, Capital Account

BoP records transactions between a country and the rest of the world, including trade in goods, services, and assets, over a specified time period, typically a year.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Balance of Payments (BoP) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Current Account Balance
text:
Current Account Balance

Key terms: Current Account, Exports, Imports

The current account balance is the difference between a country's exports and imports of goods and services, plus net income and transfer payments.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Current Account Balance in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Capital Account Balance
text:
Capital Account Balance

Key terms: Capital Account, Assets, International Transactions

The capital account balance records international transactions of assets, such as purchases and sales of stocks, bonds, and real estate, between residents and non-residents of a country.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Capital Account Balance in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Balance of Payments Surplus/Deficit
text:
Balance of Payments Surplus/Deficit

Key terms: Balance of Payments, Surplus, Deficit, Finance

A country's balance of payments is in surplus when receipts exceed payments, and in deficit when payments exceed receipts. A deficit must be financed by a capital account surplus, selling assets, or using reserves.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Balance of Payments Surplus/Deficit in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Foreign Exchange Rate
text:
Foreign Exchange Rate

Key terms: Foreign Exchange Rate, Currency, Price

The foreign exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another, enabling comparison of international costs and prices.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Foreign Exchange Rate in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Foreign Exchange Rate
text:
Foreign Exchange Rate

Key terms: Forex Rate, Currency, Comparison

Price of one currency in terms of another, enabling international cost and price comparison.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Foreign Exchange Rate in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Demand for Foreign Exchange
text:
Demand for Foreign Exchange

Key terms: Imports, Gifts, Foreign Assets

Driven by imports, gifts, and foreign asset purchases, it decreases with a rise in foreign exchange price.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Demand for Foreign Exchange in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Supply of Foreign Exchange
text:
Supply of Foreign Exchange

Key terms: Exports, Transfers, Assets

Increased by exports, foreign transfers, and asset purchases, it increases with a rise in foreign exchange price.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Supply of Foreign Exchange in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Flexible Exchange Rate
text:
Flexible Exchange Rate

Key terms: Market Forces, Appreciation, Depreciation

Determined by market forces of demand and supply, it can lead to appreciation or depreciation of a currency.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Flexible Exchange Rate in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Fixed Exchange Rate
text:
Fixed Exchange Rate

Key terms: Government Intervention, Devaluation, Revaluation

Government sets exchange rate, intervening to maintain it, leading to devaluation or revaluation.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Fixed Exchange Rate in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Managed Floating
text:
Managed Floating

Key terms: Flexible, Fixed, Central Bank Intervention

Mix of flexible and fixed exchange rates, central banks intervene to moderate exchange rate movements.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Managed Floating in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
text:
Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)

Long-run prediction about exchange rates, adjusting for differences in price levels between countries.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) in Grade 12 Economics.

text:
National Income Identity for an Open Economy

In an open economy, exports and imports are added to the national income identity, Y = C + I + G + X - M, where NX is net exports (exports - imports).

metadata.subject: Economics

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Determinants of Imports and Exports
text:
Determinants of Imports and Exports

Key terms: imports, exports, domestic income, foreign income, real exchange rate

Imports depend on domestic income (Y) and the real exchange rate (R), while exports depend on foreign income (Yf) and R. Higher income and a lower R increase imports, while higher foreign income and a higher R increase exports.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Determinants of Imports and Exports in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Open Economy Multiplier
text:
Open Economy Multiplier

Key terms: open economy multiplier, closed economy multiplier, marginal propensity to import, autonomous expenditure multiplier

The open economy multiplier is smaller than the closed economy multiplier due to the marginal propensity to import (m), which causes a leakage in the circular flow of domestic income at each round of the multiplier process.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Open Economy Multiplier in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Effects of Changes in X and M on Equilibrium Income
text:
Effects of Changes in X and M on Equilibrium Income

Key terms: exports, imports, equilibrium income, aggregate demand

An increase in exports (X) increases demand for domestic output and equilibrium income, while an autonomous rise in import demand (M) decreases demand for domestic output and equilibrium income.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Effects of Changes in X and M on Equilibrium Income
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Effects of Changes in X and M on Equilibrium Income in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Adam Smith and Wealth of Nations
text:
Adam Smith and Wealth of Nations

Key terms: Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations, invisible hand

Adam Smith (1723-1790) is considered the father of modern economics. He wrote 'The Wealth of Nations', which introduced the concept of the 'invisible hand' of the market.

metadata.topic: Adam Smith and Wealth of Nations
