title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Aggregate Money (M3)
text:
Aggregate Money (M3)

Key terms: M3, aggregate money supply, narrow money, time deposits

M3 is a measure of aggregate money supply that includes narrow money, time deposits, and other liquid assets held by the public and banks.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Aggregate Money (M3) in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Automatic Stabilizers
text:
Automatic Stabilizers

Key terms: automatic stabilizers, unemployment benefits, progressive taxation

Automatic stabilizers are features of an economy that help to stabilize output and employment, such as unemployment benefits and progressive taxation.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Automatic Stabilizers in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Balance of Payments
text:
Balance of Payments

Key terms: balance of payments, trade, services, financial flows

The balance of payments is a record of a country's transactions with the rest of the world, including trade, services, and financial flows.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Balance of Payments in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Bank Rate
text:
Bank Rate

Key terms: bank rate, central bank, commercial banks, interest rate

The bank rate is the interest rate set by a central bank that it charges commercial banks for short-term loans.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Bank Rate in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Barter Exchange
text:
Barter Exchange

Key terms: barter exchange, goods, services, money

Barter exchange is the direct exchange of goods or services without the use of money.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Barter Exchange in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Base Year
text:
Base Year

Key terms: base year, real GDP, prices

The base year is the reference year used to calculate real GDP, with prices in the base year set to 100.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Base Year in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Bonds
text:
Bonds

Key terms: bonds, loan agreement, principal, interest

Bonds are financial instruments that represent a loan agreement between the bond issuer and the bondholder, with the issuer promising to pay back the principal and interest.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Bonds in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Required Reserves for Banks
text:
Required Reserves for Banks

Key terms: Reserve Bank of India, required reserves, liquid assets

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mandates banks to keep a certain amount of money in reserve, which they cannot lend out. This is to ensure banks have enough liquid assets to meet sudden demands for cash.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Required Reserves for Banks in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Monetary Authority Intervention
text:
Monetary Authority Intervention

Key terms: monetary authority, money market, money supply, external shocks

A country's monetary authority can intervene in the money market to stabilize money supply against external shocks, like increased foreign exchange inflow.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Monetary Authority Intervention in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Stocks vs. Flow Variables
text:
Stocks vs. Flow Variables

Key terms: stock variables, flow variables, age, income

Stock variables are defined at a point in time, while flow variables are defined over a period of time. For example, a person's age is a stock, while their income is a flow.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Stocks vs. Flow Variables in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Store of Value Function of Money
text:
Store of Value Function of Money

Key terms: store of value, money, economic planning

Money serves as a store of value, allowing people to save and use it in the future. This function helps in economic planning and decision-making.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Store of Value Function of Money
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Store of Value Function of Money in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Transfer Payments
text:
Transfer Payments

Key terms: transfer payments, income redistribution, gifts, scholarships, pensions

Transfer payments are made without any service received in return, such as gifts, scholarships, and pensions. They do not create goods or services but redistribute income.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Transfer Payments in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Unit of Account Function of Money
text:
Unit of Account Function of Money

Key terms: unit of account, money, economic transactions

Money acts as a unit of account, providing a standard measure for comparing the values of different goods and services. This makes economic transactions easier.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.topic: Unit of Account Function of Money
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Unit of Account Function of Money in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Unemployment Rate Calculation
text:
Unemployment Rate Calculation

Key terms: unemployment rate, labor force, unemployed, actively seeking work

The unemployment rate is calculated as the number of people unemployed but actively seeking work, divided by the total number of people in the labor force.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Unemployment Rate Calculation in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Value Added in Production
text:
Value Added in Production

Key terms: value added, production, intermediate goods, net contribution

Value added is the net contribution made by a firm in the production process, calculated as the value of production minus the value of intermediate goods used.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Value Added in Production in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Circular Flow of Income
text:
Circular Flow of Income

Key terms: households, firms, factors of production, income

A model showing how money flows between households and firms in an economy. Households provide factors of production (like labor) to firms, earning income. Firms use this income to buy goods and services from households, completing the cycle.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Circular Flow of Income in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | National Income Accounting
text:
National Income Accounting

Key terms: GDP, GNP, NNP, national income

The process of measuring a country's total income, expenditure, and output. It helps in understanding the economy's performance and making policy decisions.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to National Income Accounting in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Money Multiplier
text:
Money Multiplier

Key terms: money supply, reserve requirement ratio, central bank

A tool used by central banks to control the money supply. It measures how much new money is created when a bank makes a loan. The formula is: Money Multiplier = 1 / Reserve Requirement Ratio.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Money Multiplier in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Aggregate Demand
text:
Aggregate Demand

Key terms: consumption, investment, government spending, net exports

The total demand for goods and services in an economy at a given time. It's determined by consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Aggregate Demand in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Government Budget Deficit
text:
Government Budget Deficit

Key terms: government expenditure, government revenue, deficit

A situation where a government spends more money than it earns. It's calculated as the difference between total government expenditure and total government revenue.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Government Budget Deficit in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Balance of Payments
text:
Balance of Payments

Key terms: current account, capital account, balance of payments

A record of all transactions between a country and the rest of the world. It includes trade in goods and services, income from investments, and transfers of money.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Balance of Payments in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Exchange Rate
text:
Exchange Rate

Key terms: foreign exchange market, interest rates, inflation

The price at which one currency can be exchanged for another. It's determined by the foreign exchange market, which is influenced by factors like interest rates, inflation, and political stability.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Exchange Rate in Grade 12 Economics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Economics | Macroeconomic Equilibrium
text:
Macroeconomic Equilibrium

Key terms: aggregate demand, aggregate supply, full employment

A situation in which the economy is at full employment and the price level is stable. It occurs when aggregate demand equals aggregate supply.

metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Macroeconomic Equilibrium in Grade 12 Economics.
